lesson.title: Loading the shoulder: pressing, pulling, overhead, progressions
lesson.summary: Shoulders get stronger with progressive load through a range the client controls. Choose variations, progress one thing at a time, and know the signs that mean do not progress.
objectives: Choose pressing, pulling and overhead variations by range, control and goal.
Progress load, range or difficulty one at a time.
Use and define cues for the press, the row and the overhead press.
Recognise the signs that mean do not progress, at every step.

blocks.content: This lesson is for healthy adults whose shoulders tolerate training. Every progression below has its own stop rule beside it; read it before you use the progression.
For healthy adults, the 2026 position stand from the American College of Sports Medicine recommends progressive resistance training to keep improving muscle strength, size and physical performance.

content.label: Spindle policy
content.text: Your training is not treatment for a diagnosed condition. A client with diagnosed shoulder pain, or one recovering from surgery, a dislocation or a fracture, trains within the treating clinician's plan, and you do not progress that plan on your own. This is Spindle's rule for trainers, not a research finding.

content.label: Stop and refer
content.text: Check first: no pain at the current level, full control of the range, and no warning sign since the last session. If pain comes on or rises with load: Stop shoulder loading for the rest of the session. Pain that is getting worse: routine referral now; do not wait. Pain that has not improved after 2 weeks: routine referral. Anything in the urgent or emergency tiers: refer at that tier.

content.caption: Planned diagram, not available yet: the pressing, pulling and overhead progressions.

blocks.content: Push-ups, presses with dumbbells or a bar, and the landmine press are all options. Choose by the range the client controls without pain and by their goal. Define a cue before you use it: "push the floor away" asks the client to keep pushing at the top of a push-up; "bend the bar" asks for tension through the upper back before the press.

content: Progression: push-up from a raised surface, then a lower surface, then the floor.
Progression: dumbbell press through a shorter range first (stopping before the bottom), then the full range the client controls.
Progression: add load only after the current range is controlled for all reps.

content.label: Stop and refer
content.text: If pain comes on or rises, or any warning sign appears: Stop shoulder loading for the rest of the session. Pain at the bottom of a press means stop for the session, not push through. In a later session, only if no warning sign remains, try a shorter range or another variation. Pain that is getting worse: routine referral now; do not wait. Pain that has not improved after 2 weeks: routine referral. This never clears anyone and never names an injury.

blocks.content: Rows and pulldowns are the pulling options. Coach the shoulder blades to move with the arm rather than holding them locked, and keep pulling work in the programme alongside pressing.

content: Progression: supported row (chest on a bench), then an unsupported row, then heavier load.
Progression: band pulldown, then a cable or machine pulldown, then a pull-up with assistance.

content.label: Stop and refer
content.text: If pain comes on or rises, or any warning sign appears: Stop shoulder loading for the rest of the session. Pins and needles that do not go away, or no feeling in the arm or shoulder: urgent, today. Pain that is getting worse: routine referral now; do not wait. Pain that has not improved after 2 weeks: routine referral. This never clears anyone and never names an injury.

blocks.content: Reaching fully overhead involves the shoulder blade rotating upward as the arm rises.

Pick an overhead variation the client can reach and control without pain. One coach-selected order is landmine press, then half-kneeling single-arm press, then standing press. Treat it as an example, not a rule.

content: Progression: landmine press, then half-kneeling single-arm press, then standing press.
Do not progress to a vertical press until the client reaches overhead without pain and without arching the lower back to get there.

content.label: Stop and refer
content.text: If pain comes on or rises, or any warning sign appears: Stop shoulder loading for the rest of the session. A new inability to lift or move the arm themselves, without an injury: urgent, today. After a fall or impact, an arm they cannot move or a shoulder that looks out of place: emergency, now. Do not move the arm or try to put it back. Pain that is getting worse: routine referral now; do not wait. This never clears anyone and never names an injury.

blocks.content: A 2026 meta-regression found that muscle growth increases as weekly training volume rises, with diminishing returns: each extra set adds less than the one before. The 2026 ACSM position stand reports that higher volumes, about 10 or more sets per muscle each week, enhanced muscle growth in healthy adults.

A 2023 meta-analysis did not find an extra muscle-growth benefit from taking sets all the way to momentary muscular failure compared with stopping short of it. That does not show the two are equivalent: a 2024 exploratory analysis suggests muscle growth increases as sets end closer to failure.
For shoulders, add weekly sets gradually, keep a few reps in reserve on most sets, and increase volume only when the client recovers well between sessions and shows no warning sign.

content.label: Stop and refer
content.text: If pain comes on or rises, or any warning sign appears: Stop shoulder loading for the rest of the session. If pain comes on as volume rises, stop shoulder loading for the session and apply the referral rules first. Pain that is getting worse: routine referral now; do not wait. Pain that has not improved after 2 weeks: routine referral. Only in a later session, with no warning sign remaining, return to a lower volume. This never clears anyone and never names an injury.

blocks.content: Progress one thing at a time
Change range, then load, then difficulty, one at a time, and re-check the client's control at each step in a later session. If two things change and pain appears, you will not know which caused it.

content.label: Stop and refer
content.text: If pain comes on or rises, or any warning sign appears: Stop shoulder loading for the rest of the session. Severe pain in both shoulders, or new pain, swelling or stiffness in several joints at once: urgent, today. Pain that is getting worse: routine referral now; do not wait. This never clears anyone and never names an injury.

content.prompt: What does the 2026 ACSM position stand recommend to keep improving strength and muscle size in healthy adults?
options: Training to failure on every set
content.explanation: The position stand recommends progressive resistance training for healthy adults.

content.prompt: Which shoulder blade movement is part of reaching fully overhead?
options: None: the shoulder blade stays still
content.explanation: Reaching fully overhead involves upward rotation of the shoulder blade.

content.prompt: What did a 2026 meta-regression find about weekly training volume and muscle growth?
options: Growth increases with volume, with diminishing returns
Growth rises by the same amount with every extra set
content.explanation: Growth increases as volume rises, but each extra set adds less: diminishing returns.

content.prompt: What did a 2023 meta-analysis find about training to momentary failure for muscle growth?
options: No extra benefit from reaching failure, which does not show the two are equivalent
Failure training always gives more growth
content.explanation: The review found no extra hypertrophy benefit from reaching failure; that does not show equivalence, and later work suggests growth increases closer to failure.

content.label: Talk it through
content.text: During a deep dumbbell bench press, a client's shoulder starts to ache at the bottom of the set; push-ups earlier felt fine. What do you do now, and what might change in a later session?
